title: WPMS/3416/2018 of ANIL CHAUHAN Vs CHETAN MEHENDIRATTA

paras.text:
WPMS No. 3416 of 2018
Honíble Lok Pal Singh, J.
Mr. Yashpal Singh, Advocate holding brief
of Mr. Neeraj Garg, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Petitioner is invoking extra ordinary
jurisdiction of this Court under Article 227 of
the Constitution of India seeking a writ in the
nature of certiorari for quashing of the
impugned order dated 22.10.2018 passed by 1st
Addl. District Judge, Rishikesh in O.S. 92 of
2016 ìChetain Mehendiratta Vs. Anil Chauhan
& anotherî(annexed as Annexure No. 1 to this
petition).
 Brief facts of the case are that
respondent/plaintiff filed original suit seeking
decree of declaration against the petitioner that
the plaintiff is entitled to get refund of an
amount of Rs. 19,45,50,000/- alongwith
interest from the petitioner and another prayer
has been for mandatory direction that not to
transfer or alienate the land till the pendency of
the suit.
 Brief facts of the case are that an
agreement to sale was executed between
defendant no.1 and plaintiff, whereby plaintiff
agreed to purchase land of Khasra no. 1644
and 1652 of Khata Khatauni no. 225 situated
at Village Rani Pokhari Grant, Pargana Parwa
Doon, Dehradun. Thereafter, on 17.09.2013, a
fresh agreement was executed between the
plaintiff/respondent no.1 and defendant no.1-
petitioner herein and area measuring 0.7610
hectare of Khasra no.1644 was agreed to be
sold. It was further contended that defendant
no.1 received the amount from plaintiff-first
respondent. It was also contended that
defendant without obtaining consent of
plaintiff-first respondent sold part of land and
received sale consideration. Consequently, a
declaration was sought by the first respondent

that he is entitled for refund of Rs.
1,94,50,000/- alongwith interest.
 The defendant no.1-petitioner herein
filed his written statement and denied the
averments made in the plaint. He also filed an
application under Order 7 Rule 11 C.P.C.,
which was numbered as paper no. 48C2
stating therein that the agreement executed
between the parties is not duly stamped. It is
also stated in the aforesaid application that the
agreement filed by the respondent on
14.02.2013 and 17.09.2013 are not admissible
in evidence, therefore, the suit is liable to be
dismissed under Order 7 Rule 11 C.P.C.
 Heard learned counsel for the parties
and perused the material available on record.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that the trial court completely
overlooked the principal relief claimed by the
petitioner in suit and passed the order
impugned dated 22.10.2018 in improper
exercise of jurisdiction.
The Honíble Apex Court in the case of
Popat Kotecha Property Vs. State Bank of
India Staff Association reported in 2005 [7]
SCC 510 has observed that The real object
of Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code is to keep
out of courts irresponsible suits.î
In another case the Honíble Apex Court in
the case of T.Arivanandham Vs. T.V.Satyapal
reported in AIR (1977) SC 2421 & (1977) 4
SCC 467, it has observed that "by holding that
clever drafting, creating illusions of cause of
action are not permitted in law. The ritual of
repeating a word or creation of an illusion in
the plaint can certainly by unravelled and
exposed by the Court while dealing with an
application under Order 7 Rule 11(a)î.
The Court below, on a thorough
consideration of the factual aspects and correct
application of law, had correctly rejected the

application under Order 7 Rule 11 C.P.C.. This
Court is of the view that there is no illegality or
perversity in the order impugned passed by the
Court below in rejecting the application under
Order 7 Rule 11 C.P.C..
The writ petition fails and is hereby
dismissed.
No order as to costs.
The trial court may proceed further in the
matter in accordance with law.
